paragraphs.title: The Officials' Request and Jeremiah's Answer

answers: The people
King Zedekiah
The king of Babylon
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that King Zedekiah sent them to Jeremiah.
easy.q: Who sent Pashur and Zephaniah to Jeremiah?

answers: Build a wall
Enquire of the Lord for them
Lead them in battle
easy.explanation: They asked Jeremiah to enquire of the Lord for them.
easy.q: What did the messengers ask Jeremiah to do?

answers: Zedekiah
Nebuchadrezzar
The priests
easy.explanation: Jeremiah told them, “Thus shall ye say to Zedekiah.”
easy.q: To whom did Jeremiah tell the messengers to deliver his words?

answers: To ask for legal advice
To ask the Lord to remove the enemy
To appoint new military leaders
medium.explanation: They asked Jeremiah to seek the Lord’s help against Nebuchadrezzar and the besieging army.
medium.q: Why did the officials come to Jeremiah?

answers: Jeremiah sent the king, and then the officials came
The officials asked Jeremiah for help, and then he told them to speak to the king
The king of Babylon sent the officials to Jeremiah
medium.explanation: The officials first brought their request, and Jeremiah then instructed them to deliver his message to Zedekiah.
medium.q: What is the correct order of events?

answers: He was ignoring the king
He was answering the officials but directing his message to the king
He wanted the officials to remain in the city
medium.explanation: Jeremiah spoke to the messengers but instructed them to deliver God’s word to Zedekiah.
medium.q: What does Jeremiah’s statement, “Thus shall ye say to Zedekiah,” show?

answers: They asked for help from the Lord, while Jeremiah gave them a message about their situation
They asked for judgment, while Jeremiah offered them a new army
They asked to leave the city, while Jeremiah forbade it
challenge.explanation: The officials sought divine help, but Jeremiah did not promise a miracle; he gave them the Lord’s answer.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between the officials’ request and Jeremiah’s response?

answers: To show who sent the message and who carried it
To show that they were all kings of Judah
To distinguish Judah’s army from Babylon’s army
challenge.explanation: Zedekiah was the sender, while Pashur and Zephaniah were the messengers.
challenge.q: Why are both Zedekiah and the two officials named at the beginning of the passage?

answers: The king sent two officials to him
The messengers left the city walls
The messengers asked to speak with the king of Babylon
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the king sent two officials to Jeremiah.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Jeremiah’s visit was an official royal communication?

paragraphs.title: God Turns the War Against Jerusalem

answers: The people of Jerusalem
The king of Egypt
The priests only
easy.explanation: The Lord said He would turn the weapons in their hands against them and into the midst of the city.
easy.q: Against whom would Jerusalem’s weapons be turned?

answers: Famine only
A great pestilence
Exile only
easy.explanation: The inhabitants, both man and beast, would die of a great pestilence.
easy.q: What would strike the inhabitants of the city?

answers: Their enemies and those who sought their life
The priests
The people of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: They would be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar and their enemies.
easy.q: Into whose hand would Zedekiah, the people, and the survivors be delivered?

answers: The weapons are turned against the city, pestilence comes, and the survivors are delivered to the enemy
The city is saved, and then the enemy arrives
The people leave the city, and a new army is formed
medium.explanation: The passage describes weapons turned against Jerusalem, death by pestilence, and eventual delivery into the enemy’s hand.
medium.q: What sequence of judgments is described in this passage?

answers: Power and strength
Peace and mercy
Secret action without force
medium.explanation: The expression describes a powerful and forceful action.
medium.q: What does “with an outstretched hand and with a strong arm” emphasize?

answers: To show that Jerusalem will defeat the Chaldeans
To emphasize the severity and completeness of the judgment
To explain why the Chaldeans will leave the city
medium.explanation: The Lord’s opposition shows how serious and decisive the judgment against the city will be.
medium.q: Why does the Lord say that He Himself will fight against Jerusalem?

answers: Weapons intended for defense would become part of the city’s judgment
The people would receive new weapons
The Chaldeans would give their weapons to the citizens
challenge.explanation: The weapons in Jerusalem’s hands would not protect the city; they would be gathered into its midst as part of the judgment.
challenge.q: What is the significance of turning Jerusalem’s weapons against the city?

answers: The king only
The soldiers only
Man and beast
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 specifically says that both man and beast would die.
challenge.q: Who is explicitly included in the plague’s destruction?

answers: That the enemy would act mercifully
That those delivered to the enemy would receive no compassion
That the city would remain independent
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording stresses the absence of pity or mercy toward those handed over.
challenge.q: What does “he shall not spare them, neither have pity, nor have mercy” emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Way of Life and the Way of Death

answers: The way of riches and the way of poverty
The way of life and the way of death
The way of war and the way of peace
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I set before you the way of life, and the way of death.”
easy.q: What two ways did the Lord set before the people?

answers: He would live safely
He would die by sword, famine, or pestilence
He would be delivered to the king
easy.explanation: The person who remained in the city would die by the sword, famine, or pestilence.
easy.q: What would happen to the person who remained in the city?

answers: He would live
He would be burned in the city
He would remain under siege
easy.explanation: The verse says that the person who went out and fell to the Chaldeans would live.
easy.q: What would happen to the person who went out and fell to the Chaldeans?

answers: Because the person who leaves may survive
Because the person who leaves will conquer Babylon
Because the person who leaves will remain in the city
medium.explanation: The one who goes out to the Chaldeans will live, and his life will be preserved.
medium.q: Why is leaving the city called “the way of life”?

answers: His life will be taken
His life will be preserved, like spoil rescued from danger
He will receive the city
medium.explanation: The expression means that the person’s life will be spared.
medium.q: What does “his life shall be unto him for a prey” mean in this context?

answers: It would be given to the king of Babylon and burned with fire
It would immediately be rebuilt
It would remain outside the conflict
medium.explanation: The Lord said that the city would be given into the king of Babylon’s hand and burned.
medium.q: What would happen to the city itself?

answers: Remaining inside the city does not bring life, while leaving to the enemy leads to life
Leaving the city is dangerous while remaining is safe
Both those who leave and those who remain receive the same promise
challenge.explanation: Although leaving means falling to the Chaldeans, it is the path that leads to survival.
challenge.q: What is the central paradox in the Lord’s instruction?

answers: It says that the city will be saved if people remain
It says that the city is appointed for harm, so remaining there is dangerous
It removes the need to choose
challenge.explanation: The city is set for evil and will be burned, so remaining there offers no safety.
challenge.q: How does verse 10 reinforce the distinction between the two ways?

answers: Leaving means surrendering to the enemy, but it is better than remaining in the city
The Chaldeans become allies of Jerusalem
Those who leave never meet the Chaldeans
challenge.explanation: The person who leaves submits to the Chaldeans, yet that submission preserves his life.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that going out is described as falling to the Chaldeans but still leads to life?

paragraphs.title: Justice for the House of David and a Warning to Jerusalem

answers: The house of David
The king of Babylon
The Chaldean army
easy.explanation: The command is addressed to the house of David.
easy.q: To whom was the command to execute judgment given?

answers: The oppressor
The priest
The prophet
easy.explanation: The house of David was told to deliver the spoiled from the hand of the oppressor.
easy.q: From whom was the spoiled person to be delivered?

answers: Water
Fire
Snow
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will kindle a fire in the forest thereof.”
easy.q: With what would the Lord kindle a fire around Jerusalem?

answers: To rescue the spoiled from the oppressor and prevent the Lord’s fury
To enlarge the city’s territory
To strengthen Babylon’s army
medium.explanation: The command to practice justice was connected with rescuing the oppressed and avoiding judgment.
medium.q: Why was the house of David commanded to execute judgment?

answers: Their location and fortified habitations
Help from the king of Babylon
Their departure from the city
medium.explanation: They asked who could come against them or enter their habitations, showing confidence in their position and defenses.
medium.q: What were the people of Jerusalem trusting in?

answers: Actions
Houses
Weapons
medium.explanation: “Doings” means actions or deeds, so the Lord would punish them according to their deeds.
medium.q: What does the word “doings” mean in “the fruit of your doings”?

answers: Failure to practice justice and evil deeds bring the Lord’s fury and judgment
The judgment was intended to start the fire
There is no connection between justice and punishment
challenge.explanation: The passage connects evil conduct with the Lord’s fury and the consuming fire.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the command for justice and the warning of fire?

answers: Their belief that their location and fortifications would protect them
Their claim that they must leave for the Chaldeans
Their claim that they belonged to the house of David
challenge.explanation: The Lord warns the inhabitants not to trust in their habitations or fortified position.
challenge.q: What false confidence does the prophet challenge in the people’s words?

answers: The Lord will repay them according to their actions
The Lord will praise them for their actions
The Lord will remove the results of their actions
challenge.explanation: The statement means that their punishment will correspond to their evil deeds.
challenge.q: What does “I will punish you according to the fruit of your doings” mean?
